title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Garden on 1973-04-02

ai_review.summary: A solid (source unknown) recording captures a brisk 1973 Hamilton show highlighted by the rare “Mind Left Body Jam” transition between China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, an extended Here Comes Sunshine jam and warm closing harmonies.
ai_review.review: Fans praise this 1973 Hamilton performance for its energetic pacing and several standout moments – the unique chord transition featuring Phil, Keith and Bob, a smoky China Cat Sunflower/I Know You Rider segue, an expansive Here Comes Sunshine jam, and a heartfelt closing with We Bid You Goodnight. No reviewer flags any serious audio problems, though the exact source (soundboard vs. audience) isn’t identified.

ai_rating.rationale: Four detailed reviews are uniformly positive about the musical performance; no recording flaws are reported, leading to a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers did not mention any sound‑board or audience issues, so the audio is presumed listenable but its exact source and fidelity are unspecified.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider (featuring “Mind Left Body Jam” transition)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The show is noted for a slightly fast tempo, tight segues (e.g., Weather Report Suite into Eyes) and generous improvisational space, especially on Here Comes Sunshine.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia receives praise for his vocal harmonies and a heartfelt send‑off at the close of the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass work is highlighted as part of the splendid chord transition with Keith and Bob.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s rhythm guitar contributes to the praised chord transition linking China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux is mentioned for his role in the smooth chord transition and extended jam sections.
